answer: Each identity locks a 75-credit bond to one violet vertex post. At dawn it files the post's shadow length and vertex angle. An auditor recomputes the shadow from the dawn solar-angle table and checks the serial: a shadow off by over 3% burns the bond, and one serial filed twice burns both. Filing costs 41 first, plus 7 per extra identity, so the 1000th costs 7034; 1000 fakes pay 3,537,500 plus 75,000 locked. A rented-post ring fails because one serial at one dawn cannot serve two sites; duplicates burn both bonds. An honest agent files once for 41 and reclaims its bond.
